public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1206

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1206](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1206)
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math.
  (1980), 89-115.
- [GGK26] M. Garaev, F. Garayev, and S. Konyagin, *On Sidon sets with squares, cubes, and quartics
  in short intervals*. arXiv:2602.08807 (2026).
- [GaKo24] Gabdullin, M. R. and Konyagin, S. V., *Trigonometric polynomials with frequencies in the
  set of cubes*. Math. Notes (2024), 336--340.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos1206

/--
Does $\{1,2^3,\ldots,N^3\}$ contain a Sidon set of size $\gg N$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_1206.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ N in Filter.atTop, ∃ S : Finset ℕ,
      S ⊆ (Finset.Icc 1 N).image (fun n => n ^ 3) ∧
      IsSidon (S : Set ℕ) ∧ c * (N : ℝ) ≤ (S.card : ℝ) := by
  sorry

/--
Is there an infinite set $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ of positive density such that $\{a^3 : a\in A\}$ is a Sidon set?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_1206.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ 0 < A.lowerDensity ∧
      IsSidon ((fun a : ℕ => a ^ 3) '' A) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1206

reformulations.difference: The source (erdosproblems.com) says "an infinite set A ⊂ ℕ of positive density". The Lean uses `0 < A.lowerDensity`, keeps a redundant `A.Infinite`, and allows 0 ∈ A (A : Set ℕ). A reader might expect natural density (`Set.HasPosDensity`) or upper density. Those readings are not equivalent to lower density in general: a set with positive lower density need not contain a subset with a positive natural density, e.g. ⋃_k [x_k, 2x_k] with x_{k+1} = 4x_k.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Erdős's original wording in [Er80, p. 109] is "is there a sequence a_t < Ct so that the sums a_i^3 + a_j^3 are all distinct?". For an infinite A = {a_1 < a_2 < ...}, the condition "∃ C, ∀ t, a_t < C t" is equivalent to positive lower density. (⇒) The count of A below b is at least ⌊b/C⌋. (⇐) Take b = a_t, where the count is t−1 ≥ (δ/2)a_t for large t; the finitely many small t are handled by enlarging C. Allowing 0 ∈ A does not matter: removing 0 keeps A infinite, keeps the lower density, and a subset of a Sidon set is Sidon. `IsSidon` of the cube image is exactly "the sums a_i^3 + a_j^3 (i ≤ j) are all distinct", since cubing is injective on ℕ. Proved in /workspace/review/equiv2.lean with only the standard axioms (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound): `(∃ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ 0 < A.lowerDensity ∧ IsSidon ((·^3) '' A)) ↔ (∃ A : Set ℕ, 0 ∉ A ∧ A.Infinite ∧ (∃ C : ℕ, ∀ t, Nat.nth (· ∈ A) t < C * (t + 1)) ∧ IsSidon ((·^3) '' A))`. The key lemma is: for infinite A, `0 < A.lowerDensity ↔ ∃ C, ∀ t, Nat.nth (· ∈ A) t < C * (t + 1)`.

https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/discuss/1206 (via r.jina.ai; comments on Tait's thesis bound n^{8/9} and on g_k(A) ≥ g_k({1..N}))

review.notes:
I found no defects. Both statements match what erdosproblems.com/1206 poses, and their `research open` tags match the site (OPEN; the page was last edited 8 April 2026) and the teorth data.

Part (i): `∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ N, ∃ S ⊆ {n^3 : 1 ≤ n ≤ N}` with S Sidon and `c·N ≤ |S|` is the standard meaning of "a Sidon set of size ≫ N". "Eventually" is equivalent to "for all N ≥ 1": {1} is a Sidon subset, so c can be shrunk to cover the small N. The subset S is chosen for each N, which correctly keeps this finite question apart from the infinite one in part (ii). In [Er80] Erdős actually asks the stronger question G(n,3) > c·n, where G is the minimum over all n-element sets. The website poses the {1..N} version and mentions the general-A question only in a remark. The file follows the website, so this is not a defect.

Part (ii): The lower-density reading is the right one. Erdős's own wording, "a_t < Ct", is exactly positive lower density (proved in Lean; see reformulations). A natural-density reading (`HasPosDensity`) would be a different and stronger requirement. An optional improvement: one docstring sentence citing Er80's "a_t < Ct" would stop future readers from "fixing" this to `HasPosDensity`, as was done for Erdős 330 in PR #4762.

Checks run: `decide` confirms `IsSidon` of {1^3..11^3} and fails for {1^3..12^3} (1729 = 1^3+12^3 = 9^3+10^3). The GGK26 results are about short intervals, and the best known lower bound for a Sidon subset of the cubes is about N^{8/9} (Tait, cited in the site comments). So neither part is settled, and neither Lean statement is trivially provable or refutable.
